title: Roadmap Towards Quantum Entanglement Positron Emission Tomography (QE-PET)
authors: Paweł Moskal, Shiva Abbaszadeh, Harmanjeet Singh Bilkhu, Peter Caradonna, Pragya Das, Praveen Gurunath Bharathi, Ana Marija Kožuljević, Zdenka Kuncic, Deepak Kumar, Mihael Makek, Marek Nowakowski, Siddharth Parashari, Kaustav Prasad, Gregory R. Romanchek, Sushil Sharma, Kenji Shimazoe, Ewa Stępień, Sodai Takyu, Miwako Takahashi, Mizuki Uenomachi, Ritesh Verma, Taiga Yamaya
abstract: Annihilation photons are quantum entangled in their polarization, a property that is not accessible in state-of-the-art clinical Positron Emission Tomography (PET). This roadmap describes the current status of research in the emerging field of quantum entanglement applications involving these photons for medical diagnosis. It outlines the underlying physics phenomena and the development of detector systems that can serve as a foundation for future Quantum Entanglement PET (QE-PET) scanners. These scanners will be capable of utilizing the entanglement between annihilation photons by measuring their Compton scattering on electrons. This roadmap comprises up-to-date experimental results on the study of quantum entanglement and the decoherence of annihilation photons, alongside the current theoretical understanding of these phenomena. The methods and detector technologies described herein are being developed (i) in order to enhance standard PET imaging by suppressing random coincidences in the reconstruction of annihilation site density distributions, (ii) in order to establish the degree of quantum entanglement as a diagnostic biomarker for tissue pathology and oxygenation, and (iii) in order to elaborate a method for pH imaging. Whether entanglement-based imaging and pH mapping can be successfully translated into clinical practice remains an open question and a subject of exciting ongoing research. This roadmap serves as an invitation to the scientific community to join this burgeoning field.
summary: This roadmap details the development of Quantum Entanglement PET (QE-PET), which aims to improve standard PET imaging by measuring the quantum entanglement between annihilation photons. By characterizing this entanglement, researchers propose new diagnostic biomarkers related to tissue oxygenation and pH mapping. While promising, translating these sophisticated quantum measurements into clinical scanners remains a significant ongoing challenge.
main_problem: The goal is to advance Positron Emission Tomography (PET) by leveraging the quantum entanglement inherent in annihilation photons, leading to a novel modality called Quantum Entanglement PET (QE-PET). This aims to overcome limitations like random coincidences and improve diagnostic capabilities.
main_result: The study establishes that quantum correlation is preserved even when one photon undergoes Compton scattering, allowing the degree of quantum entanglement ($	ext{CQE}$) to be measured as a potential diagnostic biomarker for tissue pathology or oxygenation.
method: The research combines theoretical modeling of entangled photon states with descriptions of advanced detector systems (e.g., crystal scintillators, semiconductors) capable of measuring polarization and Compton scattering angles simultaneously.
model_or_system: The physical system is the annihilation of an electron-positron pair into two back-to-back photons ($	ext{511 keV}$). The theoretical framework models the quantum state using entanglement measures like $	ext{CQE}$ and analyzes how this correlation changes upon interaction with matter (Compton scattering).
key_observables: Degree of Quantum Entanglement ($	ext{CQE}$), angular correlations ($C(	heta_S)$), relative angle ($\varphi$), and the energy spectrum of scattered photons.
important_parameters: Scattering angles ($	heta_S$), coincidence rates, and the specific physics of annihilation mechanisms (direct vs. positronium).
main_assumptions: The primary open question is the successful translation of entanglement-based imaging into routine clinical practice due to low detection sensitivity.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate event reconstruction in prototype scanners, polarization/Compton scattering planes, various annihilation processes, and plots showing how $	ext{CQE}$ and correlation measures depend on the Compton scattering angle ($	heta_S$).
paper_structure: The paper functions as a roadmap, first establishing the physics background (entanglement preservation during scattering), detailing necessary detector technologies, presenting theoretical observables ($	ext{CQE}$, $C(	heta_S)$), and concluding with the potential diagnostic applications (oxygenation mapping, pH imaging).
why_interesting: This work bridges quantum optics/information theory directly into applied medical physics. The ability to use fundamental quantum properties like entanglement as a measurable biomarker for biological processes is highly relevant to open quantum systems research.
